$comment: Specs KNOWN to fail an attempt and pass on retry. The point is not to
excuse them — it is to make a NEW flake distinguishable from a long-known
one, because on a green shard the two are byte-identical in the log.
ci.yml's 'Name the failing specs' step annotates a known entry as a
::notice (unchanged) and an UNLEDGERED flake as a ::warning. That split is
deliberate and narrow: the step's own comment records that annotating every
green-run flake as an error was measured on run 35427726541 and reverted,
because a step that cries wolf on every green run is one people learn to
ignore. A warning only on something genuinely new is the opposite of that.
Matching is on SPEC FILE + TITLE SUBSTRING, never a line number: a comment
added above a test moves its line (measured — entity-detail-layout went
from :24 to :51 inside one PR) while the test is unchanged.
Deleting an entry is correct the moment a spec is fixed or removed. The
guard asserts every entry's spec file still exists, so a deleted spec
cannot leave its excuse behind. It cannot assert the flake has stopped —
absence is not observable from one run — so that review is a human one.

flakes.title: asset detail page renders the shell
flakes.reason: MEASURED 2026-10-21 with a navigation BASELINE (#2131), and the result RETIRES the shared-shape explanation below rather than confirming it. Run 39639555647 / job 119368293674, main at 0bad11c2d (a descendant of 0e61bf5ce, so the baseline was live). This spec read `NAV DELTA : spa 3 -> 4 (+1), history 4 -> 5 (+1)` and then `the URL ROLLED BACK to a non-matching route` — url /t/acme-corp/assets, rows 3. So the gesture DID commit a client navigation and it was then undone. The entry's long-standing claim that 'the App Router transition is DROPPED, not slow' is therefore WRONG for this occurrence: nothing was dropped, something navigated back. The destination had also issued its RSC fetches (8 requests for the target URL, 30-171ms, all completing). CRITICALLY, the same run captured the data-table-platform entry (#1700) as `spa 3 -> 3 (+0)` — ZERO navigations committed. One run, one commit, two captures, OPPOSITE answers, so the two entries do NOT share a mechanism and #1329's reading of them as one detail-page family does not hold. n=1 per entry: the delta is a definite statement about that occurrence, not a rate, and 'rolled back' names what the counters show rather than a cause — no mechanism is offered here, deliberately. Two previous mechanisms on this issue were withdrawn (the `navigation entries: 1` reading, which counted DOCUMENT navigations only; and the selection-toolbar story, which rested on a multi-line parsing artefact and was reverted in #2127), so a third plausible story is not what this needs. Occurrence rate, from CI's own ::notice annotations over the last 13 main runs with an E2E job: 2 runs carried a ledgered flake, this spec once. PRIOR HISTORY, now superseded as an explanation but kept because it is why the entry exists: the dropped-transition shape was attributed to `ServiceWorkerRegistrar` reloading on every `controllerchange` (a first install is one, since sw.js called self.clients.claim() unconditionally and every Playwright context is a first visit), fix shipped 2026-10-14; that fix is live and this entry survived it.

flakes.title: Tasks row double-click navigates to detail
flakes.reason: MEASURED 2026-10-21 with a navigation BASELINE (#2131), and the result RETIRES the shared-shape explanation below rather than confirming it. Run 39639555647 / job 119368293674, main at 0bad11c2d (a descendant of 0e61bf5ce, so the baseline was live). This spec read `rows BEFORE gesture: 1`, `NAV DELTA : spa 3 -> 3 (+0), history 4 -> 4 (+0)` — ZERO client navigations committed by the gesture — url still /t/acme-corp/farm-tasks, rows 1. So the push NEVER HAPPENED: not 'started and dropped in flight', which is what every earlier capture was read as. Earlier captures printed these counters as CUMULATIVE absolutes (3, 4), which cannot distinguish that from three earlier navigations, and two readings built on them were withdrawn for exactly that reason. `rows BEFORE gesture` equals `rows`, so the row set did not change under the gesture either and the under-populated-table story stays dead. CRITICALLY, the same run captured the entity-detail-layout entry (#1076) as `spa 3 -> 4 (+1)` followed by a URL ROLLBACK — a committed navigation that was undone. One run, one commit, two captures, OPPOSITE answers, so these two entries do NOT share a mechanism despite carrying near-identical reason text until now, and no single cause explains both. n=1: a definite statement about that occurrence, not a rate. The capture also showed `rows CHECKED: 0` beside a selection toolbar labelled '1 selected' — the diagnostic flags that label as STICKY rather than live, and the toolbar mechanism was retracted and reverted in #2127, so it is recorded here as an observation and NOT revived as a hypothesis. Occurrence rate, from CI's own ::notice annotations over the last 13 main runs with an E2E job: 2 runs carried a ledgered flake, this spec once. PRIOR HISTORY, kept because it is why the entry exists: same dropped-transition attribution as #1076 (the ServiceWorkerRegistrar first-install reload), fix shipped 2026-10-14, live, and this entry survived it.

flakes.title: task detail header — task.key is copyable via CopyText
flakes.reason: RE-POINTED 2026-10-15 from #1329, which is CLOSED: its cause (the ServiceWorkerRegistrar first-install reload) was real and its fix shipped 2026-10-14, but the same shape recurred afterwards in a sibling spec and exhausted all three attempts, so the explanation does not cover this family any more. #1862 carries that evidence. A pointer at a closed issue reads as tracked while nothing tracks it (#1803). Original note follows. --- Clicked a task row, `waitForURL(/farm-tasks\/[a-z0-9]+$/)` timed out at 30s having stayed on the list. The SAME task-detail route as the data-table-platform entry above, reached by a single click instead of a double-click — which is why #1329 reads this set as a detail-page first-render shape rather than a per-spec bug. It EXHAUSTED all three attempts on #1323 attempt 1 and then passed cleanly on attempt 2 of the identical commit, so retry-exhaustion does not distinguish a flake from a real break in either direction. FIX SHIPPED 2026-10-14 for a mechanism that produces exactly this shape, so if this entry is still here at the review date it has survived that fix and the explanation is spent. `ServiceWorkerRegistrar` reloaded the page on EVERY `controllerchange`, and a first install is one: `sw.js`'s activate handler calls `self.clients.claim()` unconditionally, and on a first visit there is no incumbent to wait for, so the worker activates and claims immediately. Every Playwright test gets a fresh context, so every test was a first visit and took a full reload mid-test. A reload discards a pending App Router transition, which is this family's shape — the click is made, the navigation never completes, and the page is still on the list. This is NOT a new hypothesis: it is the cause already recorded for #1329 against theme-first-paint, identified 2026-10-11. That fix was spec-local (`serviceWorkers: 'block'`), correctly for a first-paint measurement, and left the mechanism live for every other spec. The listener now reloads only when the page was ALREADY controlled at mount or the operator consented. Not claimed as proven for this entry — the earlier service-worker experiment on #1076 measured INCONCLUSIVE because the flake did not fire in that window, and absence still cannot be observed from one run. Hence the nearer review date rather than a prune.

flakes.title: F — read-only invariant: AUDITOR cannot create tenant-level records
flakes.reason: RE-POINTED 2026-10-25 from #1862 to #2313, on the owner's ruling, because this spec CANNOT exhibit #1862's shape: that family is a dropped client transition, and this test's ledgered case does only a `safeGoto` document navigation plus two visibility waits — there is no click-then-transition in it, so there is no pending transition to drop. That also retires #1329 as a candidate for it, since a controllerchange reload discards a PENDING transition and this test has none. Its failures are load timing or hydration, which needs a different instrument: navigation counters are undefined across a document load, because the document is replaced and they reset. Everything below is the entry as it stood, unaltered. --- RE-POINTED 2026-10-15 from #1329, which is CLOSED: its cause (the ServiceWorkerRegistrar first-install reload) was real and its fix shipped 2026-10-14, but the same shape recurred afterwards in a sibling spec and exhausted all three attempts, so the explanation does not cover this family any more. #1862 carries that evidence. A pointer at a closed issue reads as tracked while nothing tracks it (#1803). Original note follows. --- Observed on #1316. A DIFFERENT test from the `G — CISO creates a 2nd tenant` entry above, in the same file: #1329 listed ciso-portfolio :183 and :214 together, and only :214 was ledgered, so :183 was still reading as a NEW flake on every occurrence. Ledgered separately rather than by widening G's title, because a title that matched both would excuse any future test in this file.
